title: When words feel too necessary
meaning: You can develop a conversation generously, while the pleasure of attention can make a reply feel like necessary proof of closeness.
text: Sometimes you want to hear an affectionate sentence again although you already understand it. In Vishuddha, the Empress in the physical position appears through generous speech: encouraging a story, saying something kind and finding words for a small event. The Empress in energy nourishes the exchange through a sincere interest in your shared life. The Devil in emotions shows how the sweetness of a response can become binding. A reply starts to feel necessary before you can feel wanted. Conversation stays lively, yet its emotional weight may become unexpectedly great.

For example, you exchange amusing photographs and little messages during the evening. An ordinary exchange grows into a cosy conversation, pleasant to continue around other things. **A warm word is especially precious when it remains freely given.** A sentence can bring pleasure without requiring the next confirmation immediately. Attention then nourishes your connection, and a brief interval leaves intact the good things already said that evening.

The difficulty begins when another question seems necessary to test your closeness until the desired answer finally settles you. Conversation gradually becomes a wait for the right reaction to each message. Warmth remains what you want, but becomes harder to feel without repetition. The freedom to reply later restores the voluntary nature of a word and allows attention already received to carry weight.
